nations.name: Caddo Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with offices in Binger; the Nation describes ancestral homelands in present-day Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas

facts.text: The Nation's history says a removal treaty signed on July 1, 1835 involved Caddo living in northwestern Louisiana under principal chief Tsauninot.
The Nation recounts that a Caddo group on Texas's lower Brazos reservation was evacuated in 1859 to avoid a massacre by Texas frontiersmen.
facts.evidence: emergency evacuated by the U.S. Indian Agent

facts.text: The Nation dates the beginning of its current language program to August 1, 2022. This institutional milestone does not date the start of Caddo language preservation.
The Nation's Historic Preservation Department describes work in repatriation and consultation, and publishes separate procedures for Section 106 and NAGPRA requests.
